task: make the spine proprioception gate satisfiable again

inputs.gate: spine_cycle_apply proprioception gate -- refuses to write while any of seven derived artifacts is stale
inputs.reported: nothing wrong; the loop refused hourly and said nothing

label.root_cause: graphify-out/graph.json and GRAPH_REPORT.md are two of the seven checked artifacts, and tools/refresh_all.py deliberately does not rebuild them -- so the gate could only ever be satisfied by hand, and the refusal was silent
label.fix: scripts/graph_refresh_no_llm.py -- runs `graphify update .` (code re-extract, no model, no quota) then `cluster-only` to regenerate the report from the rewritten graph, in that order so extract alone cannot leave the report 49 sources stale

evidence.detected_by: reading the gate's artifact list against what refresh_all actually rebuilds
evidence.verified: tools/artifact_freshness.py: all 7 artifacts current, graph/report consistent (nodes=687101 clustered=True), spine gate open

inputs.first_failure: rc=-1, single reported line 'EOF marker not found' after 1522s
inputs.surrounding_output: discarded -- only the last line of each step was kept

label.root_cause: graphify classifies a file by SUFFIX alone, then hands it to a parser chosen by that suffix; a ProPublica HTML block page saved with a .pdf extension threw 'invalid pdf header' / 'EOF marker not found', and the script's one-line diagnostic cap discarded every earlier line so what failed was unknowable
label.fix: two changes -- (1) graph_refresh_no_llm.py now persists full per-step output to logs/graph_refresh_step<N>.log on every exit path; (2) the mislabelled file was renamed .pdf -> .html

evidence.detected_by: re-running with full output captured, then the recovered step-1 log naming the file and the pypdf error
evidence.verified: run 3: `update .` rc=0 in 2463s, `cluster-only` rc=0 in 8s, graphify-out current, done in 2475s rc=0

task: stop a standalone refresh colliding with the scheduled cycle

inputs.writer_before: only spine_cycle_apply._launch_graph_refresh(), i.e. the cycle spawning the child

label.root_cause: the scheduled cycle consults only the marker to decide whether a pass is in flight; a standalone ~31 minute run never claimed it, so the next hourly fire would launch a competing re-extract over the same 101k-file tree
label.fix: write_marker() now claims the slot inside the script itself (in the exact '<time> <pid>' shape the reader parses, so a live pid still distinguishes a real pass from a corpse), cleared on every exit path in finally

evidence.detected_by: tracing who writes the marker vs who launches the refresh
evidence.verified: run 3 claimed the marker at start (pid 19532) and it was absent after exit; no second pass started during the 2475s run

label.root_cause: an L1-level audit module and the expansion worm shared a basename, so basename-based resolution could bind the wrong module
label.fix: renamed the L1 module to src/CORE/l1_wiring_audit.py and updated its three call sites (src/CORE/neural_loop.py, scripts/genome_adaptation_audit.py, tests/test_learning_closure.py); the expansion worm's own wiring_audit.py is untouched

evidence.verified: CORE.l1_wiring_audit imports; 48 tests pass (test_learning_closure + test_spine_graph_remediation); fs_hygiene 'OK: no regression vs logs/fs_baseline.json'

task: audit the tree for other files that could abort a graphify parse

inputs.question: how many other files lie about their extension?
inputs.instrument: tools/audit_parseable_files.py -- content-based magic-byte check over graphify's parseable binary formats

label.root_cause: graphify's classify_file dispatches on path.suffix alone, so any suffix that lies sends the wrong parser at the bytes; nothing in the tree was checking this
label.fix: new tools/audit_parseable_files.py: per-extension signature predicates, --deep opens every .pdf with pypdf, --check exits non-zero, --fix renames text-wearing-a-binary-suffix; tests/test_audit_parseable_files.py pins both directions

evidence.detected_by: running the audit across 565 parseable-binary files
evidence.verified: 0 corrupt PDFs; 0 office/paper mismatches (the formats parsed inline and so able to abort); only 63 JPEG-as-PNG and 3 zero-byte MP4, all in vendored/archived or gitignored output -- images/videos are not parsed inline by `update`, so they cannot abort a code-extract; vendored fixtures deliberately NOT renamed because onnxruntime's own tests reference them by name

task: make the gate loud at the source, not only in one caller

inputs.reported_before: the refusal is a returned dict; the gate recorded a beat, but the event store is not stdout

label.root_cause: the ~30h refusal was fixed in spine_cycle_apply's wrapper, but night_shift and train_today read the same dict and printed 'proposals=0' -- success-shaped -- so the same outage would still be invisible through them
label.fix: emit a logging.warning in SpineCycleWorm.run_cycle's refusal path (the module's existing _logging convention), so every caller surfaces it whether or not it inspects the dict; night_shift and train_today additionally label a refused apply explicitly; tests/test_spine_gate_warning.py pins the warning, the reason text, and that apply=False observation is never refused

evidence.detected_by: grep of every run_cycle caller and reading their status lines
evidence.verified: 12 tests pass (test_spine_gate_warning + test_audit_parseable_files); 37 pass across the visibility and learning-closure suites
